newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Alliance says won't give NZ's Labour blank cheque.
newsitem.headline: Alliance says won't give NZ's Labour blank cheque.

text.p: Jim Andertson, leader of New Zealand's left-wing Alliance Party, said on Tuesday his party would not give Labour and New Zealand First a blank cheque if they formed a coalition.
"The Alliance is not a footstool for any party and we will not give a blank cheque," he told a news conference.

"If there is no concession to the Alliance, if the policies of Labour and New Zealand First are quite different and less progressive than what they promised in the election campaign, then they would be very unwise to count on Alliance support," he said.
The National and Labour parties are vying to win support from NZ First to be in a position to form a government after Saturday's inconclusive election.
Anderton said of seven possible options for government outlined by NZ First leader Winston Peters the people wanted to know which were the practical ones.
The Alliance will on Wednesday publish an issues paper on its position for forming a government with Labour and NZ First.
He said if Labour and New Zealand First come to an agreement then they must make a joint statement on policy which would have to be put to the Alliance.
Labour had approached the Alliance but NZ First had not.
Anderton said he believed NZ First favoured forming a coalition with the National Party. Then it would have to make an agreement with only one party.
"I think the New Zealand First hierarchy had been lining themselves up to go into coalition with National for some time."
"Its policy position has been modified so significantly in recent months, that that is the only conclusion you can draw."
He said NZ First had softened its stance on foreign investment, market rents for state houses and the labour laws to be more appealing to the National Party.
